requirements.verifier_assertion: Rubric item 1 (VLM judge): a full-viewport black overlay with a centered spinning blue-border circle is shown first, then fades out cleanly after the Earth texture loads, revealing the globe and HUD.
Rubric item 2 (VLM judge): a photorealistic textured Earth sphere is surrounded by a glowing blue atmospheric rim, over a starry space background.
must_include: atmospheric glow shell at 1.25x the Earth's radius

requirements.verifier_assertion: Rubric item 3 (VLM judge): many colored flight-path arcs span between cities, and small airplane icons/particles move smoothly along those arcs.
must_include: HSL hue keyed off departure longitude
InstancedMesh of up to 34,297 plane billboard instances
green, blue, purple, gray, yellow, orange, red, light-gray

requirements.verifier_assertion: Rubric item 4 (VLM judge): dragging rotates the globe smoothly with inertia; zooming is limited so the camera never clips through Earth or flies absurdly far.
must_include: spin the globe around with the mouse

requirements.verifier_assertion: Rubric item 5 (VLM judge): dat.GUI panel exists with groups such as Plane, Animation, Flight, Lighting and Brightness, and changing values visibly affects the scene.
Rubric item 6 (VLM judge): toggling 'show paths' or 'show planes' hides or reveals those elements; toggling the lighting option switches globe between day and night shading.
Rubric item 7 (VLM judge): a small FPS monitor panel is displayed after loading and its value fluctuates with rendering.
Rubric item 8 (VLM judge): footer shows an attribution link on the left (GitHub author credit) and a live latitude/longitude readout on the right that updates as camera moves.
must_include: live camera-center lat/lng readout in monospace text

requirements.verifier_assertion: Rubric item 9 (VLM judge): the camera performs a short cinematic ease-in before resting in the default orbit position.
must_include: camera eases smoothly from 1.2x distance to 1.0x distance over 2 seconds

requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh short-circuits to reward=1.0 when a file '.oracle_pass' exists at $WORKSPACE/.oracle_pass and starts with the exact string 'ORACLE_PASS <instance_id>'. Only the solution/solve.sh should ever write this — a real agent's solution must NOT create it.
